---

## 7. REUSE OPPORTUNITIES

Things a PDP build should be using rather than rebuilding:

1. **`PdpProductInfo` + its theme recipe** — `overrides/app/components/pdpProductInfo/index.tsx` and
   `overrides/app/theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts`. Name / price / sanitized description / model
   line / style code, all test-id'd, all styled through `useMultiStyleConfig`. **This is the reference
   implementation of the repo's styling convention** — copy its structure for every new PDP component.
2. **`Breadcrumb`** — `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx`. Wired to live `useCategory`
   data, `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`, `aria-current="page"` on the terminal crumb, `aria-hidden`
   separators, exports its own `BreadcrumbCategory` type. Import it **relatively**.
3. **`ZimmPageToolbar`** — `ui-kits/atoms/zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx`. Already has `recently-viewed`
   and `section-title` variants built and **unused**. A "You May Also Like" / "Recently Viewed" PDP
   section should use `variant="recently-viewed"` rather than a new wrapper.
4. **`extractModelLine`** — `overrides/app/utils/productData.ts`, plus its 5 passing tests.
5. **`ProductWithSizeFit`** — `overrides/app/types/commerce.ts`. Extend this file for new `c_*` fields;
   don't re-derive the Product type per component.
6. **`PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH`** — exported from `product-detail/index.tsx:14` and already consumed by
   the story. Any gallery/options layout work should import it, not restate `360px`.
7. **`ProductPage` POM** — `e2e/support/pages/ProductPage.js`. Already has `goToProduct()` with the 20s
   SFCC-API gate, `selectVariant()`, `addToCart()`, `getFirstBreadcrumbCategoryLink()`, and locators for
   `product-price` / `product-description` / `product-style-code` / `product-model-info` /
   `sale-price` / `original-price` / `out-of-stock` / `cart-drawer`. **`sale-price`, `original-price`,
   `out-of-stock` and `cart-drawer` locators exist but nothing renders those test-ids yet** — they are a
   pre-agreed contract for the next PDP slice. Use those exact test-ids.
8. **SFCC-91's `pdpColourSwatches`** — 189 lines of component + 256 lines of Vitest + 204 lines of
   stories + an 883-line spec at `.docs/specs/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches.md`, plus the multi-colour
   SKU fixture in `e2e/fixtures/products.js`. **Rebase-and-adopt, do not rewrite.** Two caveats: it
   predates the `pdpProductInfo` theme-recipe refactor (rebase conflict guaranteed in
   `pdpProductInfo/index.tsx`), and it needs relocating to `ui-kits/` + a theme recipe to match convention.
9. **`.claude/rules/overrides.md`** on `origin/feature/f2r-component-registry` — the pre-flight checklist
   (default export, internal-consumer grep, `forwardRef`, Chakra deep-merge audit, prop-superset pattern,
   `vendor.d.ts` ambient rule). If PDP work overrides any SFCC component, run that checklist. Consider
   asking for it to be merged to `develop`, since `overrideStyling.md` already links to it and the link
   is currently dead.
10. **`overrides/app/utils/sfccImage.ts` — `proxyImageUrl(url)`.** **This one matters a lot for the
    gallery.** It rewrites an absolute SFCC static-asset URL to `/mobify/proxy/<path>…` by matching the

    browser access to the Demandware host "is typically blocked by Cloudflare WAF outside of the

    unchanged) on a relative or malformed URL. **[V]**

### Gaps the takeover should decide about explicitly

- **The gallery column is a coloured empty box** (`index.tsx:56`). Everything image-related is unbuilt.
- **`overrideStyling.md` vs `uikit-components.md`** — two mutually exclusive styling models on two
  branches (§2c). Get a ruling before writing components.
- **`ui-kits/` has one component and no rules doc on `develop`** (§2b/2c). Both `pdpProductInfo` and
  SFCC-91's `pdpColourSwatches` sit outside it. Either relocate them or stop calling ui-kits settled.
- **The story duplicates the page shell** (`index.stories.tsx:43-65` vs `index.tsx:48-88`) because
  Storybook has no `CommerceApiProvider`. Adding one to `.storybook/preview.tsx` would delete the
  duplication — but `.storybook/` is **Tier 1 frozen** (`frozenFiles.md` > Test & Tooling Config), so
  that needs Integration/SI Partner approval.
- **Error handling diverges from base**: base throws `HTTPNotFound`/`HTTPError` (`index.jsx:194-209`),
  ours renders an inline message (`index.tsx:66`). SEO consequence — a bad `productId` returns HTTP 200
  with an error string instead of a 404. AGENTS.md calls SEO a top requirement; worth raising.
- **`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is Squad A territory** (`.claude/rules/squadA.md:5`, draft),
  and the shared product components (`product-tile/`, `display-price/`, `image-gallery/`,

  (`protectedFiles.md` > Shared Product Components). Overriding any of them crosses a squad boundary

427	## 7. Honest overall assessment
428	
429	**Verdict: a solid *component* base sitting on an unsafe *integration*. Keep the components, rework the page and the two override-shadow decisions.**

431	### What is genuinely good — keep it
432	- **`PdpProductInfo` + its theme recipe is exemplary.** Correct `useMultiStyleConfig` pattern, `Zimm`-prefixed and registered, every escape hatch documented with a written exit path. This is the pattern the rest of the branch should be migrated to.
433	- **Accessibility was taken seriously and is real, not claimed.** `h1` for the product name, `nav`/`ol`/`li` breadcrumb semantics, `aria-current="page"`, `aria-hidden` separators, and a Storybook `play` that actually asserts tab order (`breadcrumb/index.stories.tsx:46-52`).

442	3. **The `Breadcrumb` override silently restyles the PLP.** It shadows a shared SFCC component and is not a faithful port — the PLP breadcrumb loses its chevron separators and its theme config. Nobody asked for that and the PR body doesn't mention the PLP at all.
443	4. **The `Pages/PDP` story is a copy-paste of the page**, so the one artefact reviewers will actually look at is not the thing being reviewed.
444	
445	### Effort to make it good
446	Roughly a day of focused work, and it is mostly *decisions*, not code:
447	
448	- **10 minutes:** `npm run lint:fix` (all 5 errors auto-fixable); delete the redundant `.gitkeep` and the dead `: null`.
449	- **Half a day:** move `Breadcrumb` and `ZimmPageToolbar` styling into `theme/components/*.ts` recipes (the author already knows how — `3e1686b` is the template); `react-intl` the four hardcoded strings; make `ZimmPageToolbar`'s padding responsive; add the missing per-site SKUs or a hard configuration error.
450	- **Half a day:** extract a presentational `PdpLayout` so the page and the story stop duplicating; add a Vitest for the breadcrumb-assembly/degradation logic; move `index.test.ts` → `utils/productData.test.ts`.
451	- **Blocking, needs humans not code:** Integration sign-off on `isomorphic-dompurify` (or swap for a lighter sanitizer); a product/Squad-A decision on the base-PDP replacement scope; UI Designer notification for the two Tier 2 theme files; a squad-lead call on the PDP ownership move.
452	
453	### Takeover recommendation
454	Do **not** rebase-and-continue on top of this. Land the four blocking decisions first — dependency approval, PDP replacement scope, breadcrumb-shadow strategy, theme-file owner sign-off — because two of them (scope, breadcrumb) may delete or restructure a meaningful slice of the code. The component layer (`PdpProductInfo`, `ZimmPageToolbar`, the stories, the `.feature`) is worth carrying forward almost verbatim.

## 7. Honest overall assessment

**Verdict: a solid *component* base sitting on an unsafe *integration*. Keep the components, rework the page and the two override-shadow decisions.**

### What is genuinely good — keep it
- **`PdpProductInfo` + its theme recipe is exemplary.** Correct `useMultiStyleConfig` pattern, `Zimm`-prefixed and registered, every escape hatch documented with a written exit path. This is the pattern the rest of the branch should be migrated to.
- **Accessibility was taken seriously and is real, not claimed.** `h1` for the product name, `nav`/`ol`/`li` breadcrumb semantics, `aria-current="page"`, `aria-hidden` separators, and a Storybook `play` that actually asserts tab order (`breadcrumb/index.stories.tsx:46-52`).
- **Storybook coverage is complete and correctly categorised** — all four surfaces, `play` functions only where there's interaction.
- **Gherkin-first E2E workflow followed** — `.feature` before spec, correct `@pdp`/`@SFCC-89` tags on all 10 tests, sensible page-object locators using accessible selectors first.
- **The `generateRegistry.mjs` consumer-count fix is a real, well-reasoned improvement** (specifier anchoring instead of substring grep, plus a single file-walk instead of N subprocesses). It happens to be unrelated to SFCC-89.
- **`tsc` and Vitest are green.**

### What makes it not mergeable as-is
1. **A Tier 1 file was changed after the PR body itself said it was blocked pending approval.** That is the single most serious thing here — not because dompurify is wrong (it's the right call for `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), but because the process gate was identified and then walked through. It also drags in 16 MB / jsdom on the SSR path with no bundle-budget verification.
2. **Merging this removes add-to-bag and all SEO metadata from the PDP.** Whether that's in scope for "static product information" is a product question no one has answered in the PR. It cannot merge to `develop` without an explicit answer.
3. **The `Breadcrumb` override silently restyles the PLP.** It shadows a shared SFCC component and is not a faithful port — the PLP breadcrumb loses its chevron separators and its theme config. Nobody asked for that and the PR body doesn't mention the PLP at all.
4. **The `Pages/PDP` story is a copy-paste of the page**, so the one artefact reviewers will actually look at is not the thing being reviewed.

### Effort to make it good
Roughly a day of focused work, and it is mostly *decisions*, not code:

- **10 minutes:** `npm run lint:fix` (all 5 errors auto-fixable); delete the redundant `.gitkeep` and the dead `: null`.
- **Half a day:** move `Breadcrumb` and `ZimmPageToolbar` styling into `theme/components/*.ts` recipes (the author already knows how — `3e1686b` is the template); `react-intl` the four hardcoded strings; make `ZimmPageToolbar`'s padding responsive; add the missing per-site SKUs or a hard configuration error.
- **Half a day:** extract a presentational `PdpLayout` so the page and the story stop duplicating; add a Vitest for the breadcrumb-assembly/degradation logic; move `index.test.ts` → `utils/productData.test.ts`.
- **Blocking, needs humans not code:** Integration sign-off on `isomorphic-dompurify` (or swap for a lighter sanitizer); a product/Squad-A decision on the base-PDP replacement scope; UI Designer notification for the two Tier 2 theme files; a squad-lead call on the PDP ownership move.

### Takeover recommendation
Do **not** rebase-and-continue on top of this. Land the four blocking decisions first — dependency approval, PDP replacement scope, breadcrumb-shadow strategy, theme-file owner sign-off — because two of them (scope, breadcrumb) may delete or restructure a meaningful slice of the code. The component layer (`PdpProductInfo`, `ZimmPageToolbar`, the stories, the `.feature`) is worth carrying forward almost verbatim.

395	Mapping **402 → `base`** and **1440 → `xl`** is a **decision to be confirmed, not a measured fact.**

426	everything else uses `text/default` `#191919`. No repo token matches. Almost certainly a design slip.
427	
428	**D. Product name style differs by breakpoint.** `Default/h3-strong` (−0.12px) desktop vs

442

444	variable, so they will drift. Cosmetic in the DS, no repo action.

447	desktop info column `218`, gallery↔column gap `179`, right pad `142`. Expected for a composed page;

# SFCC-89 — PDP Static Product Information: Figma design specification

**Source file:** `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (Zimmermann_Final-Approved-Designs) — composed page states.
**Target node given:** `3087:15747`.
**Extracted:** 2026-08-22. Read-only; no repo file and no Figma node was modified.

---

## 0. Method and tool caveats (read this before trusting any number)

Two of the four requested tools were **unusable in this session**:

| Tool | Result |
|---|---|
| `get_metadata` (with nodeId) | Works, but the target subtree serialises to >315 KB and the MCP SSE transport truncates it. **Deterministic failure**, retried twice. |
| `get_screenshot` | Works. Used throughout. |
| `get_variable_defs` | **Fails**: `"You currently have nothing selected."` It resolves against the Figma **desktop app's current selection**, not the `nodeId` argument. |
| `get_design_context` | **Fails**: same "nothing selected" error, same reason. |

Because `get_variable_defs` and `get_design_context` were unavailable, all variable, typography and
layout data below was obtained instead via **read-only Plugin API traversal** (`use_figma` with
scripts that only read and `return`). This is a *better* source than `get_design_context` for this
purpose — it returns resolved variable names, collections, modes and per-mode values rather than
pre-rendered Tailwind — but it is a substitution worth stating.

**If you want `get_design_context` / `get_variable_defs` output**, the user must select the node in
the Figma desktop app first; nothing in this environment can do that.

Two further transport quirks, recorded so the next person doesn't rediscover them:
- The SSE channel truncates responses at a **variable** cap (~19 KB–315 KB observed). All traversal
  was paginated.
- **A non-ASCII character in some layer names breaks the SSE JSON encoding outright** (frames named
  `PDP - Denim Applique<U+?>Mini Dress`). Every script below sanitises names to ASCII. A script that
  returns raw `node.name` for that range fails 100% of the time.

### Measurement rules applied

- **TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, not a CSS line box.** Every TEXT height below is labelled
  and must **not** be turned into a CSS `height` or used to file a mismatch.
- **A FRAME that hugs a TEXT child inherits that cap-height artifact.** This bites here: the
  accordion row frames report `218x9`. That 9 px is the text cap-height, not a row height. For those,
  use the **row pitch** (gap + measured offsets), which is artifact-free.
- FRAMEs/INSTANCEs with fixed or content-independent sizing (column widths, button, icons, gallery)
  report real boxes and **are** directly CSS-comparable.

---

## 1. What this screen is, and the node tree

**`3087:15747` is not a screen — it is a `PAGE`** named `└– 🟢  PDP`, containing **67 top-level
children** and spanning 108649 × 41878 px of canvas. The green marker in the page name appears to be
this file's "approved" convention (unverified — a naming convention, not metadata).

### ⚠️ FRAME WIDTH IS NOT A BREAKPOINT

The repo's actual breakpoints (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts`, registered in
`theme/index.ts`):

```
base 0em · sm 30em (NOT used) · md 48em = 768px · lg 62em (NOT used) · xl 80em = 1280px · 2xl 96em (NOT used)
```

There is **no 860 or 1024 breakpoint token in the theme** (grepped: zero hits for `860`). If the
brief's "768 / 860 / 1024" came from somewhere else, it is not the Chakra breakpoint scale.

Mapping **402 → `base`** and **1440 → `xl`** is a **decision to be confirmed, not a measured fact.**

**The real gap: the 768–1280 range (`md`) is undesigned for this column.** The design jumps from a
342 px full-bleed mobile block to a fixed 218 px desktop column beside a 900 px gallery. Nothing
specifies what happens in between. Note that the DS `Grid` collection *does* define a Tablet mode
(`grid-columns` 8, `grid-margin` 24, matching the repo's `md` values) — so tablet is tokenised but
not drawn. **This needs a designer answer before implementation.**

`gridSystem.ts` hardcodes a single `columnGap: '1px'` for all breakpoints and its comment asserts

`gridSystem.ts` is **Tier 1** — do not touch; raise with the UI designer. Columns (10/8/4) and
margins (0/24/30) match the repo exactly.

`44` (the largest structural gap) are the important ones. Ask: round to `xl`/`2xl` (24/32) and
`3xl` (40), or add new tokens?

**B. Undesigned tablet (768–1280).** No 1023-ish frame exists. Column behaviour between 342-full-bleed
and 218-fixed is unspecified. Blocking for a responsive implementation.

**C. `#000000` on two labels.** "Size Guide" and "Find your size" use unbound pure black while
everything else uses `text/default` `#191919`. No repo token matches. Almost certainly a design slip.

**D. Product name style differs by breakpoint.** `Default/h3-strong` (−0.12px) desktop vs
`Default/Heading 3` (−0.16px) mobile. Pick one.

**E. `body2Strong` letter-spacing is −0.12px in the repo but −0.14px in Figma.** Unlike the others
this has an unambiguous fix — `letterSpacings['2xs']` already exists and is exactly −0.14px. Still a
Tier 1 file (`typography.ts`), so it needs the designer/owner, but it is a defect not a gap.

**F. Icon sizes with no token.** Accordion chevron `9 x 9` (×4, both breakpoints) and the size
chevron (`9` desktop / `13` mobile). `iconSizes` only has 20/16/12. The 9/13 split between
breakpoints looks unintentional.

**G. Wishlist icon differs by breakpoint** — 16px glyph desktop (in a 24px 4-padded tappable box)
vs bare 20px mobile. Both map to existing tokens, but the mobile one has **no padding**, giving a
20 x 20 hit target — **below the WCAG 2.2 AA 24 x 24 minimum target size (2.5.8)**. Flag to design.

**H. Unbound brand colours.** `#f6f4f1` and `#ffffff` match repo tokens by value but carry no Figma
variable, so they will drift. Cosmetic in the DS, no repo action.

desktop info column `218`, gallery↔column gap `179`, right pad `142`. Expected for a composed page;
listed for completeness.

**Matches the repo exactly (no action):** `heading3`, `price`, `body2`, `caption`, `linkLg`,

# PR #57 / SFCC-89 audited against the FED Lead Playbook

**Reference doc:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/fedLead-playbook.md` (800 lines, read in full).
**Subject:** PR #57 `feat(pdp): SFCC-89 — PDP UI static product information`, author **JhoanDelaCruz**,
branch `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information` @ `d526ad1`.
**Audit date:** 2026-08-22. **Read-only** — no repo file, PR, ticket or Figma node was modified.

> ⚠️ **The playbook is a local-only document.** It must never be cited in a PR comment, commit
> message, code comment, or Jira/Confluence page. Every finding below that needs to be raised
> externally has a **citable repo equivalent** — see §F for the mapping table. Use those.

---

## (a) Verdict

The playbook has an answer for more of this than you would expect — and almost all of its answers sit
on the **reviewing** side, which is the side that did not happen. Play 5's three-surface review
(diff + preview environment + Figma) would have caught both P0s inside the hour it budgets: the MRT
preview URL was posted on the PR on 2026-08-18 and, four days later, no human has opened it, so a
route that 500s on **every** SSR request and an info column that is **142px** off the approved design
both survived to a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` decision that is 100% CodeRabbit. On the build side the picture
is genuinely mixed and the author deserves better than the diff suggests: he **followed** the playbook's
hardest habits — override-first rather than bespoke, a Storybook story for every exported component,
real (not claimed) accessibility, and Play 9's "flag it in-code and raise it, don't silently pick a
number" on the one value he could not source. He **broke** documented rules in three places that matter
(a Tier 1 dependency his own PR body said was blocked, an override that discards the base wiring the
override-first argument rests on, and a shared-component shadow that restyles the PLP), and he **hit
gaps the process never covered** in at least six more (lint gated by nothing, `auditTokenUsage.mjs`
mandated but non-existent, a `ui-kits` convention that exists only on an unmerged branch and
contradicts `develop`, `CODEOWNERS` and `squadA.md` disagreeing about who owns his page, three live
tickets claiming his scope, and a blocking attribute story that has not reached the sandbox he is
tested against). Of the four decisions you have deferred, the playbook **prescribes an answer** for
one (page composition — Play 1's own worked-examples table says add-to-bag already exists in
`product-view`), **prescribes a procedure but not an answer** for two (ticket scope → Jas reworks the
card, Play 8; design/token gaps → Kiera, Play 9), and is **completely silent** on the fourth: there is
no takeover guidance anywhere in 800 lines.

---

## (b) Process failures, against what the playbook actually says

**Classification key.** `VIOLATED` = the playbook says it and it wasn't done. `FOLLOWED` = credit where
due. `SILENT` = the playbook has nothing on this; the citable rule is elsewhere (§F). `NOT-IN-FORCE` =
the playbook postdates the event — see the fairness note after the table. `PREDICTED` = the playbook
names this exact failure mode as a risk and it happened anyway.

### B1 — Reviewing side (this is where the process broke worst)

| # | What happened | Playbook says | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The MRT preview environment was posted on the PR by `github-actions` on **2026-08-18T20:51:44Z** and, as of 2026-08-22, **no human has opened it**. Each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group, or it silently falls back to the full suite."* L709 puts the Tier 1 exception with **you**, not him. | **FOLLOWED** — the follow-up is the Lead's |

Its closest lever is Play 1's lookup table, L94: the registry's **`Consumers`** column — and `.claude/registry/components.md:15` does report **`Consumers: 3`** for `Breadcrumb`.    `{name}.styles.ts` + Emotion `<Global>`, where `overrideStyling.md` mandates Chakra props + a theme
   recipe. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` contains exactly one component. Playbook L184–224
   presents this as *"decided"* and *"settled"*; on `develop` it is neither.
5. **Two governance files disagree about who owns his page**, and a third disagrees about its tier —
   see §D.

   refinement-stage findings as **NOT-IN-FORCE**, not as violations.

---

## (c) What the playbook prescribes for each of the four deferred decisions

### C1 — Page composition: does the PDP override replace the base page?

**The playbook prescribes an answer, not just a procedure — and the answer is "no, compose it".**

Play 1 makes override-first the default for one specific reason, L116–121:

> *"**default to overriding the base component, not writing a new one.**
> The reason is not tidiness — it's that an override **inherits the wiring for free**. Override
> `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart modal, bundle
> handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of those has to
> be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed, and none of it is visible in the story points."*

and its worked-examples table (L107) already names add-to-bag as base capability. A 95-line override
that renders a grey `<Box>` where `ProductView` used to be is the bespoke-equivalent outcome the play
exists to prevent, arrived at through the override mechanism. Play 1's second-order note, L123–127, is
the other half:

> *"PWA Kit's resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component SFCC's own base
> components already import means the whole base template inherits your version** — no call sites
> touched."*

That cuts both ways, and here it cuts against: two independent shadowing mechanisms (route order at
`overrides/app/routes.tsx:37`, and the mirrored path redirecting base `routes.jsx`'s own import) mean
deleting the route entry does not undo it.

**Play 7 makes the decision yours, not the author's**, L556:

> *"M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout,
> design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX."*

and the ownership table, L689, assigns *"Component reuse, override-vs-build calls, PR quality"* to
**You**. So this is not an escalation — it is a call you make and record.

**Concretely, what the playbook implies you should decide:** the PDP page override composes the base
`ProductView` (or an override of it) and layers `PdpProductInfo` + the breadcrumb toolbar around it,
so add-to-bag, swatches, quantity picker, gallery, `<Helmet>`, `HTTPNotFound` and `<Island>` deferred
hydration all survive. If instead the deliberate call is "SFCC-89 ships a reduced PDP and SFCC-91/92
restore the rest", that is a legitimate product decision — but the playbook's decision-recording rule
(L625) says it must land *"on the story **and** into the relevant Confluence page — not just the
thread."* Right now it is recorded nowhere, and the PR body does not mention it.

**Where the playbook is silent:** it has no review question for *"does merging this remove something
the storefront has today?"* Review questions 0–9 (L439–451) cover reuse, override-vs-bespoke, tokens,
abstractions, base capability, a11y, stories, Figma parity and ui-kit placement. Nothing covers
subtraction. See §E-G1.

### C2 — Ticket ownership and scope (SFCC-89 vs SFCC-737 vs SFCC-723 vs SFCC-578)

**The playbook prescribes a procedure and a named owner, not an answer.**

The owner is **Jas**, per the ownership table, L687:

> `| Story content, AC, Figma links on the card | **Jas** | Rework the card, don't patch it verbally — Play 8 |`

and the mechanism is Play 8's, L617–620 — written about Figma links but stated as a general principle
about card correctness:

> *"**Action:** where a card's Figma links are wrong, stale, or point at the wrong frame, go back to
> **Jas** and ask for the card to be reworked with correct links rather than clarifying it verbally to
> one developer. A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — the thing BA and
> QA both read — still wrong."*

Three tickets claiming one deliverable is a card-content defect of exactly that shape: fixing it in a
PR comment repairs your understanding and leaves SFCC-737 sitting at *Ready For Review* claiming
"product name, description, model description, style code" verbatim.

**Play 8 also gives you the precedent for the shape of the fix**, L597 (Shop the Look):

> *"Four names in circulation for possibly two things … **Resolve to one name per capability before
> estimating**"*

and L596 (Recommendations): *"Raise 647; don't create tickets."* Applied here: raise SFCC-737 and
SFCC-723 with Jas, get one owning ticket per deliverable, do **not** create a new reconciliation
ticket.

**Play 2 gives you the substantive argument to bring**, L245–253 — its component-build vs
page-composition table, and responsibility #16 (*"Separate component-build effort from page-composition
effort in estimates"*). The playbook's own model says the component build and the page assembly are
different stories. That is the same rule Confluence 04.71 states, and it lands the `pdpProductInfo`
component build on SFCC-737 and the assembly on SFCC-89.

**Where the playbook is silent:** it never contemplates a duplicate ticket in a *different epic owned
by a different squad*, and it has no concept of an overdue story or of a story built ahead of its
design-lock date. Play 2's challenge list does contain the tripwire, L264 —
*"`- [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column)`"* — and Play 9 L668 predicts
exactly this outcome:

> *"04.7's status column marks components Done on *design* confirmation, which doesn't imply the
> implemented API matches. Worth agreeing what 'Done' means in that column, since story writers are
> reading it as readiness."*

Product Content is 🟡 *Done, minor update required*. It was read as readiness. The playbook called it.

### C3 — The sanitiser and the Tier 1 dependency

**The playbook does not prescribe anything here. State that plainly rather than stretching it.**

Guardrails, L709, is the only Tier 1 clause and it is scoped by its own examples:

> *"**Tier 1 files.** You hold tier-1-approver / admin, so the verified-session exception applies — you
> can proceed after naming the file and the reason. Relevant to Play 5's two proposed rules
> (`.coderabbit/`, `.eslintrc.js`) and to `.github/workflows/`."*

L711 lists the four absolute files; `package.json` is not among them. So on a literal reading you
*could* self-authorise. **Do not read it that way**, for two reasons the playbook does not state:

1. **AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 is a different rule with a different authority.** The verified-session
   exception is written against Hard Rule #2 (Tier 1 *files*) and turns on membership of
   `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. Hard Rule #7 says *"Never add or remove packages from
   `package.json` without **integration team** approval"*, and `frozenFiles.md` names the owner as
   *Integration / SI Partner — #integration*. Tier-1-approver status is not integration-team approval.
   AGENTS.md's "When to Stop and Ask a Human" table is unambiguous: *"A new package dependency is
   needed → Stop. Integration team must approve."*
2. **AGENTS.md > Performance > Dependencies** requires the comparison first: check what is already
   installed, evaluate whether it can satisfy the requirement, present the recommendation, wait for
   approval. No such comparison exists anywhere in the PR. The repo has four production dependencies
   total; this adds a fifth that drags jsdom into the SSR bundle, and `vendor.js` is now at **95.4%**
   of its 550 KB budget (524.74 KB) with ~25 KB of headroom.

**The playbook has no performance or bundle-budget content at all** — Play 5's gate zero (L360–364)
stops at `tsc`, lint and vitest. See §E-G7.

**What is genuinely prescribed** is only the shape of the escalation: the ladder (L80–88), which for a
dependency reads *"is there an existing capability → an existing pattern → new, justify it out loud"*,
and L52–54's *"Do as much as we can and flag the rest… An invented value becomes a defect **and** a
design-system divergence."* Both point the same way: this needs an Integration decision, on the record,
before merge — and the technical case for it changed on 2026-08-22, because the dependency is now known
to be the **cause of P0-B**, not merely an unapproved add. `isomorphic-dompurify`'s node entry
instantiates JSDOM at module-evaluation time, and `pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:2` imports it at module
scope; that is the `__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__` TDZ error on every SSR request. Take that to
Integration as the finding, not the licence question.

### C4 — PR takeover strategy

**The playbook is silent. There is nothing about taking over, rewriting, or pushing to another
developer's open PR anywhere in 800 lines.** See §D for the one transferable precedent and for what
has to come from repo files instead.

---

## (d) Takeover etiquette and ownership, applied

### D1 — What the playbook actually offers

**Nothing direct.** Grepped for `take over / takeover / handover / reassign / the author / someone
else`: no hits in a takeover sense. Three fragments constrain you, and one precedent transfers:

- **L717 — the constraint on you:** *"**Commits and PRs** only on explicit request — not as a 'natural
  next step' after finishing work."* This is AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15 restated. Investigating PR #57 is
  not authorisation to commit to it. You have deferred the decision; that means the branch stays as it
  is until you are asked.

> are dropping — components, hooks, SSR status codes, cache headers, `<Island>` boundaries, `<Helmet>`.
> If the list is non-empty, it goes in the PR body and it needs a product decision recorded on the
> story, not a reviewer's assumption. Citable rule: AGENTS.md > Rules > Minimal changes."*

> **Proposed — Play 1, one line under "Override-first":**
> *"Override-first buys you the wiring. Throwing the wiring away and keeping the override is the worst
> of both — the blast radius of an override with the coverage of a stub."*

### G2 — A bot-only `CHANGES_REQUESTED` with no human review **(confirmed gap)**

The playbook does not mention CodeRabbit anywhere. Its "Already mechanical — don't spend review time on
it" table (L330–340) models ast-grep, semgrep, `tsc`, lint, commit-msg and the registry hook, but not a
review bot — so it has no vocabulary for *"the PR looks reviewed and has not been."* It also has no
review SLA, and no escalation for five requested teams going silent for four days.

> **Proposed — Play 5, new subsection "The bot is not a reviewer":**
> *"CodeRabbit's `CHANGES_REQUESTED` is a lint pass with opinions, not a review. Before you read its
> findings, check the review list: if every review and every thread is `coderabbitai[bot]`, this PR has
> had **zero** human review and the state you are looking at is not a review outcome. Three consequences:
> (i) treat the bot's findings as a starting point, not as coverage already achieved; (ii) the bot cannot
> see the preview environment or Figma, so every finding in the three-surface list is still outstanding;
> (iii) the bot loops — a finding raised and reverted twice (see U4 breadcrumb leaf category, reverted in
> `47ad72b` and `0ec26f9`) will be raised a third time, and per AGENTS.md the correct response is an
> in-thread reply citing the commits, not a code change.*
> *Review SLA: a requested team review that is unanswered after 2 working days gets escalated by name in
> stand-up, not re-requested silently. Four days of silence on a PR that removes add-to-bag is a process
> failure, not a queue."*

### G3 — A Tier 1 violation the author self-documented and then committed anyway **(confirmed gap)**

Guardrails (L709–711) covers Tier 1 *files* and the four absolute files. It does not cover dependency
adds, does not distinguish Hard Rule #7's Integration-team authority from tier-1-approver membership,
and has no response for the specific pattern here: **the author identified the gate correctly in his own
PR body, then walked through it.** That is a distinct and more worrying failure mode than not knowing
the rule, and it deserves a named response rather than being folded into "Tier 1 violation".

> **Proposed — Guardrails, new paragraph:**
> *"**Dependencies are not covered by your Tier 1 exception.** AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 requires
> **integration-team** approval to add or remove a package — a different authority from
> `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, and one you do not hold. Before it goes to Integration, AGENTS.md >
> Performance > Dependencies requires the comparison: what is already installed, can it do the job, what
> is the installed and bundled cost. Add `npm run test:max-file-size` to gate zero — `vendor.js` currently
> sits at 95.4% of its 550 KB budget, so one dependency is enough to break it.*
> *A separate note on a pattern seen on PR #57: where a PR body **names a gate and the change then crosses
> it anyway**, that is not a rule-knowledge problem and a comment restating the rule will not fix it. Ask
> directly what unblocked it — a verbal approval, time pressure, or an assumption that the PR gate would
> catch it — and fix that, because the same thing will happen on the next dependency."*

### G4 — Two governance files contradicting each other **(confirmed gap)**

Play 1's lookup table (L97–98) names `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and the registry as the squad/tier
sources and never mentions CODEOWNERS — the only one GitHub enforces. There is no rule for what to do
when they disagree, and no rule against changing the derived one inside a feature PR (which is exactly
what happened via `generateRegistry.mjs`).

> **Proposed — Play 1, replace the two lookup rows:**
> *"| Is it already claimed by a squad? | **`CODEOWNERS` is authoritative** — it is the only source
> branch protection enforces. Registry `Squad` column and `.claude/rules/squadA.md` are documentation
> derived from the rules files and can drift. |*
> *| What tier am I about to touch? | **`CODEOWNERS` + `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`**; registry
> `Tier` column second. |*
> *Standing check: if CODEOWNERS and the registry disagree about a path, CODEOWNERS wins for the merge
> and the divergence is its own governance change with both squad leads — never a constant edit inside a
> feature PR. Verified live example: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is Squad B / Tier 3 in
> `CODEOWNERS:159`, Squad A in `squadA.md`, and Squad A / Tier 4 in `.claude/registry/pages.md:20`."*

### G5 — A component with cross-page blast radius but no tier and no squad **(gap)**

`overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/` appears in no tier list and no squad list, yet it shadows a
component the PLP renders. The playbook's only lever is a registry column nobody is told to check for
this purpose.

> **Proposed — Play 5, add to review question 1:**
> *"Check the registry's `Consumers` count for anything you are overriding. **≥2 consumers, or any
> consumer outside the page you are building, means treat it as Tier 2 for review purposes** regardless
> of what the tier lists say — the tier lists are incomplete. And for any component SFCC's own base
> components import, the default export stays a faithful, undecorated port; brand treatment goes behind a
> named export or the theme recipe (`overrideStyling.md` > The SFCC bridge pattern)."*

### G6 — The three surfaces do not include "does the route work" **(gap)**

Play 5's three surfaces are the diff, the preview environment and Figma (L382–386), and gate zero is
`tsc` / lint / vitest (L360–364). Neither catches a route that returns 500 on SSR — which is exactly
what happened, and what unit tests (146 passing) and Storybook (27 passing) **cannot** catch by
construction, because they render components in isolation with props.

> **Proposed — Play 5, add to gate zero:**
> *"`npm run build` — then hit the preview URL for the route you changed and check the HTTP status and
> the server log, not just the pixels. Components can be individually green and the assembled page still
> 500 on the server; unit and Storybook passes are evidence for the component layer only. On PR #57 this
> would have taken one minute and would have found the blocker four days earlier."*

### G7 — Performance and bundle budgets are absent from the playbook entirely **(gap)**

Not one line on LCP, bundle size, code splitting or dependency weight, in a playbook whose §1 quality
bar is a 10-defect SOW ceiling on a luxury storefront where AGENTS.md sets a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget.
Folded into G3's proposed gate-zero addition.

### G8 — "Green CI" that ran nothing **(gap)**

Two runs on this branch (`cf17c3d`, `d904c63`, both 2026-08-20) are recorded green with **every test job
skipped** — the `since_last_remote_commit` trap — and a skipped required check satisfies the gate.
Play 5b has the right instinct at L521–522 (*"would this test still pass if the feature were broken in
the obvious way?"*) but nothing on skipped-is-green.

> **Proposed — Play 5, gate zero:**
> *"A green check mark is not evidence a check ran. `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` uses
> `since_last_remote_commit: true`, so a push that touches only docs skips every test job — and a skipped
> required check satisfies branch protection. Before trusting a green run, open it and confirm the test
> step actually executed. Also know what is **not** required: Playwright E2E and BrowserStack are not
> required checks on `develop`, so a PR can reach a mergeable state with its entire E2E suite red."*

### G9 — No takeover guidance at all **(gap — this is the one you needed today)**

> **Proposed — new Play 10, "Taking over someone else's PR":**
> *"**Before you touch it.** Commits and PRs only on explicit request (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15) — deciding
> to take over is itself the request, and it comes from the developer or the squad lead, not from having
> finished reading the diff.*
> *__Talk to the author first.__ The precedent is the F2R coordination: raise it before more work stacks
> on it, and don't discard their artifacts — the work that is right is usually most of it, and the author
> is the cheapest source of why the rest is the way it is. Ask specifically about anything that looks like
> a deliberate deviation; on PR #57, `c_sizeFit`-instead-of-`modelFit` and the leaf-category revert both
> look like errors and both have reasons.*
> *__Check their other branches.__ A dependent branch that forked from an older commit will conflict.
> Adopt it, don't rewrite it.*
> *__Decide the blocking questions before writing code.__ If a decision could delete or restructure a
> slice of the branch, land the decision first; rebase-and-continue on an undecided scope wastes the work
> twice.*
> *__Authorship and approval.__ Pushing to their branch does not make you the PR author, so you can still
> approve — which means you must be careful not to become the only approver of a change you wrote.
> `dismiss_stale_reviews: true` also means every push you make resets any approval already given;
> sequence review after your last push.*
> *__Split the PR if the tiers split.__ AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 forbids spanning protection tiers without
> confirming scope. A Tier 1 dependency change and a Tier 3 page build in one PR means one blocked
> approval chain blocks everything; separating them lets the safe two-thirds merge."*

### G10 — No handling for a story built ahead of its own readiness **(gap)**

Play 2's challenge list (L264) asks whether designs are confirmed, and Play 9 (L668) predicts that 04.7's
"Done" gets read as readiness — but neither says what to do when the answer arrives **after** the build.
SFCC-89 was due 17 Aug, is in Code Review on 22 Aug, and its design is not "ready for development" until
24 Aug.

> **Proposed — Play 2, add to the challenge list:**
> *"`- [ ] If this story is already in flight and 04.7/04.72 say the design is not locked: what is the
> 'minor update', and does it touch what has been built? Get that answer before review, not after — a
> re-work found at review costs the review budget twice.'"*

1. **Spend the hour Play 5 budgets** — open the MRT preview beside Figma at 402 and 1440. That is one

Audit written to `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/4447dd18-bbe0-4a85-aae2-6e8935bf7947/scratchpad/audit-fedlead.md`. Read-only throughout — nothing in the repo, the PR, Jira or Figma was touched.

## Condensed report

**Verdict.** The playbook covers more of this than expected, and nearly all its coverage is on the **reviewing** side — the side that didn't happen. Play 5's three-surface review would have caught both P0s inside the hour it budgets: the MRT preview URL was posted 2026-08-18 and four days later no human has opened it, so a route that 500s on every SSR request and a 142px layout error both survived to a bot-only CHANGES_REQUESTED. The author followed the playbook's hardest habits (override-first, a story per exported component, real a11y, and Play 9's "flag it in-code, don't invent a number"), broke three documented rules that matter, and hit six gaps the process never covered.

**1. Process failures.** Reviewing side is worse than the author's. VIOLATED: nobody opened the preview env (L388–391, verbatim *"There is no longer a reason to review a UI change from the diff alone — **open the environment and put it beside Figma.**"*); nobody compared to Figma (review Q8, L447); the only Lead activity in 4 days was typing `@coderabbitai full-review`, against L49 *"**Vigilance is the job, not an overhead on the job.**"*; and Lead action item 12 (set "green locally" once, to the whole team, L759–760) is still open — which is precisely why the author opened with 5 lint errors while ticking "lint passes". Author side: gate zero (L356–364), `var(--zimm-*)` in JSX at 8 sites (L416), and the PR body attributing 0-for-7 Playwright failures to sandbox provisioning — a textbook instance of Play 5b's *"a proxy reported as the finding"* (L512–513). **Followed, and worth praising:** `PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH` was flagged in-code as provisional rather than silently guessed — exactly L665–666.

**The playbook is SILENT on the three biggest items:** the Tier 1 dependency, the shared-component shadow, and the bot-only review. Their citable homes are AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7, `overrideStyling.md`'s bridge pattern, and AGENTS.md's CodeRabbit-reply rule.

**Fairness to the author:** lint/prettier/tsc are gated by *nothing* (zero matches across 15 workflows and all 3 hooks); `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` is mandated by `overrideStyling.md` and does not exist (verified); `.claude/rules/overrides.md` is cross-referenced 5× and does not exist on `develop`; the `ui-kits` convention exists only on an unmerged branch and contradicts `develop`; his design isn't locked until 24 Aug; and the playbook's own UI-build additions landed the same day his PR opened — so Plays 1/2/3 were **not in force** when SFCC-89 was drafted.

**2. The four deferred decisions.**
- **Page composition — the playbook prescribes an answer.** Play 1's own worked-examples table (L107) says add-to-bag already exists in base `product-view` (verified: `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])` at `product-view/index.jsx:401`), and override-first is justified solely because an override *"inherits the wiring for free"* (L118). A 95-line override replacing an 876-line page discards exactly that. Play 7 (L556) + the ownership table (L689) make this **your** call, not an escalation — record it per L625, on the story *and* Confluence.
- **Ticket scope — procedure, not answer.** Owner is **Jas** (L687); mechanism is L617–620: rework the card, don't patch it verbally to one developer. Precedent for the shape: L597 Shop-the-Look, *"Resolve to one name per capability before estimating"*; L596, raise the existing ticket, don't create new ones.
- **Sanitiser + Tier 1 — the playbook prescribes nothing; say so.** Guardrails L709 scopes the verified-session exception to `.coderabbit/`, `.eslintrc.js`, `.github/workflows/`; `package.json` isn't addressed. Critically, **Hard Rule #7 is a different authority from tier-1-approvers** — Integration must approve, and your admin status doesn't substitute. Take it to Integration as a *defect report*: `isomorphic-dompurify` instantiates JSDOM at module scope, which is the `__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__` SSR crash.
- **Takeover — completely silent.** Nothing on takeover anywhere in 800 lines.

**3. Takeover and ownership.** The one transferable precedent is item 15 (L772–777, the Han F2R coordination): talk to the author first, *"**Don't discard the `.styles.ts` files**"*, raise it before more work stacks on it. Two mechanics the playbook misses: `dismiss_stale_reviews: true` means every push you make resets any approval; and since Jhoan is the PR author you *could* push the Tier 1 change and approve it yourself as tier-1-approver — don't, for the reason AGENTS.md gives for the gate existing at all. **CODEOWNERS vs squadA.md is actually a three-way disagreement** (verified): `CODEOWNERS:159` = Squad B/Tier 3, `squadA.md` = Squad A, `.claude/registry/pages.md:20` = Squad A/Tier 4 — and this PR *widened* it by moving the path from `SQUAD_B_PATHS` to `SQUAD_A_PATHS` in `generateRegistry.mjs`. Play 1's lookup (L97–98) names squadA.md and the registry and **never mentions CODEOWNERS**, so following the playbook returns the wrong answer on the only surface GitHub enforces. On SFCC-578: the breadcrumb is untiered and unclaimed in *every* repo governance file while shadowing a component the **PLP** renders (verified: `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:14`) — the playbook's squad guardrail (L715) doesn't reach it, so it goes to both squad leads.

**4. Gaps.** All four candidates confirmed real, plus six more. Ten proposed additions, written as drop-in text: a review question 10 for subtractive changes; a "The bot is not a reviewer" subsection with a 2-day review SLA; a Guardrails dependency clause separating Hard Rule #7's authority from yours; CODEOWNERS as the authoritative squad/tier source; a "consumers ≥2 means treat as Tier 2" rule; a route-level HTTP check in gate zero; bundle budgets (`vendor.js` is at **95.4%**); a "green CI that ran nothing" caveat (two runs on this branch are green with every test job skipped); a **new Play 10 on taking over a PR**; and a Play 2 line for a story built ahead of its design lock.
